t: This is the equestrian statue of William III, in St James's Square. It is Grade One listed. The king, also known as William of Orange, ruled England, Scotland and Ireland from 1689 until 1702, jointly with his wife Mary until her death in 1694. The sculptor was John Bacon the Younger, and the statue is modelled on an earlier one in Queen Square, Bristol. Samuel Travers paid for it in his will of 1724, but nothing happened for seventy years. It was finally put up in 1808.
